minutes.headline: Select Board agreed to reallocate ARPA funds to the schools to narrow the budget gap; override vote deferred to March 26.
minutes.summary: The board held joint and scheduled appointments, heard a water district PFAS update, a conservation staffing plan, and a town manager report including a large trash contract increase. The main item was reallocating ARPA money to the school budget to close most of the gap to the school committee's minimum budget, with debate over whether the override still goes on the warrant and ballot. Warrant articles were reviewed, a late citizen petition was ruled not actionable, and an early-voting question was deferred pending a posted public hearing.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town secured a new three-year natural gas rate beginning December 2025, compared with the current rate.
Extending the hauler contract on current terms would bring a large price increase; the town requested a 90-day extension and will go out to bid, also considering a cart system.
Previously allocated sidewalk ARPA money would be reallocated to the schools since Chapter 90 can fund the sidewalks.
The town manager proposed pausing the pavement management plan for one year and redirecting the funds to the schools.
The superintendent listed enhanced 911, network security and Chromebook purchases as items to move onto ARPA.
Items were totaled and the remaining ARPA balance discussed, with some kept for a solar consultant at the old dump.
With ARPA and the paving money, the school budget gets close to but not fully to the needs-based minimum percentage.

budget_items.what_was_said: The school committee is asking in the capital plan for an analysis of Turkey Hill, tied to plans for TC Pasos and municipal building design.
A petition to add department funding to the override was received late and unsigned and was not actionable.

budget_items.what_was_said: The article to transfer free cash for security upgrades is expected to be withdrawn because ARPA now covers it.
Articles for sewer capital reserve and sewer OPEB transfers were described.
Annual article to appropriate from sale of cemetery lots for cemetery care.
Conservation needs more technical consultant hours than current fees provide and will review fees and seek a revolving fund.
A weekly accounts payable warrant was signed.
The water district has state revolving fund financing at zero interest with principal forgiveness, compared with bank rates.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted by roll call to move sidewalk ARPA money to the school department, plus more uncommitted ARPA money for 911, network security and Chromebooks.
The town manager proposed pausing the pavement management plan for a year and redirecting those funds to the schools; with ARPA, the schools get close to, not fully to, the minimum budget.
A decision on the override was deferred; the board set a special meeting on the override and warrant for March 26 at 7 pm.
The town manager reported that extending the trash hauler contract on current terms would bring a large increase, so the town requested a 90-day extension and will go out to bid.
A late, unsigned citizen petition to add department funding to the override was ruled not actionable, and warrant article recommendations were deferred.

why_it_matters: Moving one-time ARPA money and paving funds to the school budget narrows the gap without a tax increase, but does not close it, so residents may still be asked to vote on an override.
The trash contract will be rebid after the 90-day extension, and the larger price at the new contract could change what the town spends on solid waste and recycling next year.
watch_next: Special Select Board meeting on the override and warrant, March 26 at 7 pm.
Public hearing on early in-person voting, posted for April 2; assessors and Council on Aging revised senior exemption article due April 2.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on most votes and the main ARPA reallocation, but ours misses the 5-0-0 / 7-0-0 / 4-0-0 tallies and several attendees, and carries many garbled figures. The one thing to check is the Historical Commission item (we say "not audible", the town records a dismissal without a vote) along with the override petition amount ($265,500 vs $265,000) and the AP warrant ($291,500 vs $291,652.30).
